rules.text: When the attack payload is a perceptual input (image, audio, rendered document), show concrete examples early: one figure with a clean and an attacked input side by side and the model's responses, plus an example of every attack variant evaluated; use benign or redacted content when the real payload is harmful. A pipeline diagram does not replace these examples.

When the main contribution is a newly measured vulnerability rather than a defense, use a measurement-paper skeleton: methodology and findings first, then mechanism evidence, then the explanatory hypothesis, then a short mitigation derived from it, then confounder controls; the main table crosses models with input conditions and reports a capability metric beside ASR.

Every claim in a results paragraph must point to a figure, table or appendix item the reader can inspect; when evidence exists only as values read off a plot, redraw it and say so in the caption, or narrow the claim to what the shown evidence supports.

Draw error bars or bands only when they encode real uncertainty, such as variation across seeds or a confidence interval over test items; otherwise omit them, state the run count in the caption, and never draw zero-width error bars.

In figures comparing the same inputs with and without a treatment, give each input condition one hue, separate untreated from treated by shade or hatching, place the untreated bar first, and mark the change within each pair.
When a result curve has qualitatively distinct regimes, name each regime once with its boundary values and defining behaviour, and reuse those names consistently in later text and figures.

rules.text: Size the abstract to the target venue's norm rather than the skill's upper bound, compress the challenges into one clause, name a category instead of listing its members, and never claim that no prior work has asked the question.
Number the introduction's challenges in the order in which the approach paragraph and the paper's sections answer them, so that the tags appear in ascending order.

When a paper has both a Background and a Related Work section, give each cited idea one home: Background states only premises the method relies on, Related Work contrasts approaches, and the positioning sentence appears once.
Before finalizing the Discussion, check every forward-looking sentence and rephrase any untested generalization as a hypothesis or future work, unless an experiment in the paper supports it.

rules.text: llm_agent_security diagrams: set max_label_words = 6 (was 4). Figures in this area routinely show short prompts and model replies verbatim (jailbreak responses, refusals, injected instructions), which typically need five or six words.

In threat-model and attack-defense figures, reserve the adverse role (fill and border) for attacker-controlled actors and successful-attack outcomes; draw payloads, attack-variant lists and intermediate artefacts as neutral blocks (at most an adverse edge), never mark inputs on a path that ends safely as adverse, and if more than a third of the blocks would be adverse, demote all but the attacker and the attack outcome.

When one shared component produces different outcomes depending on its input, keep the alternatives in parallel lanes up to their outcomes: span the shared block across the lanes, repeat it per lane, or label each outgoing edge with its condition; never merge the paths into one node and fan out again unlabelled.

Draw an enumeration of variants or instances as an aligned row or column of equal-size blocks under one shared header, without an arrow per item, and place control inputs such as prompts, policies or defenses upstream of the component they act on so no edge points against the reading direction.
